item.title: Gorden Secondary school Administration building gutted this morning
item.description: Gorden secondary school administration building damaged in fire (NBC News) Acting Commander of Waigani fire station, Joseph Ungil confirmed that the challenges faced today to contain the fire at the Gorden secondary administration building was the availability of water source inside the school premises.
item.content:encoded:
Gorden secondary school administration building damaged in fire (NBC News)

Acting Commander of Waigani fire station, Joseph Ungil confirmed that the challenges faced today to contain the fire at the Gorden secondary administration building was the availability of water source inside the school premises.

Ungil said the fire truck had to go back and refill four times before they contained the fire.

The acting Commander of Waigani fire station said the Waigani Fire station received the call at 7 am in the morning and arrived at the Gorden secondary school where they saw huge flames from the administration office.

About 20 fireman who drove to the location did an assessment of the wind direction and did fire break for offensive and defensive firefighting and saved the building extension part of the administration building.

“Because the school does not have the fire hydrant where they will source the water, they had to call for backup from Boroko Fire Station.

“The Waigani Fire Station fire truck contains only 3,000 liters of water and 200 foam. So the 3,000 liters of water, when you are using it at 500 kPa, in a second, 10 liters per second goes out and 10 liters per second at 500 or 300 kPa.” Ungil said.

Ungil said the Fire service has specialized inspectors to conduct fire cause investigation and will provide brief to Papua New Guinea Fire Service headquarters.

He also advised the school principal to barricade the scene so the fire investigators will come and do the investigation.

Meantime, the school principle George Kenega declined to comment on the incident.

item.title: Police investigating death of DWU student
item.description: Madang PPC, Chief Superintendent Vakaruru Uraia (NBC News) Police in Madang are investigating the gruesome killing of a university student in the Raikos District last Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Madang PPC, Chief Superintendent Vakaruru Uraia (NBC News)

Police in Madang are investigating the gruesome killing of a university student in the Raikos District last Saturday.

"Madang CID are investigating the wilful murder of a 29-year-old Divine Word University student on Saturday night, 7th October at Aiyau Village, Astrolabe Bay, Raikos District, Madang," PPC Uraia said.

Chief Superintendent Uraia said the deceased was attacked by several assailants as he slept, suffering fatal injuries.

He added, "Investigators are now interviewing key family members and associates to establish a motive for the killing. Sorcery allegations have recently been made against the deceased by people known to him.

"The investigation is progressing, and we hope to arrest the perpetrators shortly. The deceased leaves behind his wife and three young children."

According to information sourced from DWU, the young man was a 3rd year Information Systems student and had gone home for the Christmas holiday.

He was from the Bugati area and had gone to Raikos to bring his wife and children back home for the holiday when he was killed in his sleep.

item.title: Narcotics Bureau takes drug awareness to Morobe
item.description: Shirley Kwam, Senior Juvenile Justice Officer with the Department of Justice and Attorney General, speaking to students at Omili Primary School during a drug awareness session (NBC News) The National Narcotics Bureau is taking drug awareness to communities in Morobe as it works to educate people about the dangers of drug use.
item.content:encoded:
Shirley Kwam, Senior Juvenile Justice Officer with the Department of Justice and Attorney General, speaking to students at Omili Primary School during a drug awareness session (NBC News)

The National Narcotics Bureau is taking drug awareness to communities in Morobe as it works to educate people about the dangers of drug use.

The Bureau is also planning to set up a provincial office in Morobe to improve its work with local communities and government agencies.

Director General Kiria Kotange says a two-week training and awareness program is now underway in the province.

The first week focuses on training selected participants, while the second week will involve visiting communities to share information about drugs and their effects.

The participants will be trained as narcotics ambassadors to help spread drug awareness in their own communities.

Kotange says the Bureau wants more people to understand the dangers of drugs and how drug use affects individuals, families and communities.

He says marijuana remains one of the common drugs used in the country, while other drugs such as methamphetamine and cocaine are also a concern.

Kotange says the Bureau works with police and other government agencies to address drug-related problems.

He explains that police are responsible for arrests and law enforcement, while the Bureau focuses on awareness, prevention and working with communities.

However, limited funding remains a major challenge for the Bureau as it tries to reach more people across the country.

The planned Morobe office is expected to help the Bureau work more closely with local authorities and communities.

Through the awareness program, the Bureau hopes to encourage people, especially young people, to stay away from drugs and help prevent drug use in their communities.

item.title: Callan officiate closure at doors
item.description: Students from Kulangit receiving their end of year gifts, from teachers, supported by parents (NBC News) Callan Inclusive Education Resource Centre in Kavieng has taken a different approach to its 2026 academic year-end closure, delivering its school closing program directly to students and their families through a door-to-door initiative.
item.content:encoded:
Students from Kulangit receiving their end of year gifts, from teachers, supported by parents (NBC News)

Callan Inclusive Education Resource Centre in Kavieng has taken a different approach to its 2026 academic year-end closure, delivering its school closing program directly to students and their families through a door-to-door initiative.

The first-of-its-kind initiative comes amid the prolonged El Niño drought, which has severely affected water supplies and placed additional pressure on families caring for children with special needs.

To mark the closure, Chairman and outgoing Catholic Education Secretary Fr. Mark Kombeng, officially closed the teaching and Learning at the centre, before the delivery yesterday.

A total of 57 students attending the centre this year has received 114 water containers, official school closure letters and special end-of-year gifts through the program.

The water containers were delivered from Monday, November 9, while teachers continued the door-to-door visits yesterday, personally handing over gifts and school closure letters to families.

Program Coordinator Miss Joanne Beno says, the first-of-its-kind initiative was organized to ensure every student received their end-of-year gift and that no family was left uninformed about the school's early closure.

item.title: Morobe provincial Tutumeng chamber set for upgrade
item.description: The Morobe Provincial Government is planning to improve the Tutumeng chamber in Lae, with a focus on modern meeting facilities, better seating and improved support for media coverage. Governor Rainbo Paita says the proposed improvements will address the current needs of the Morobe Provincial Assembly, including the installation of modern audio-visual equipment and a Hansard recording system.
item.content:encoded:
The Morobe Provincial Government is planning to improve the Tutumeng chamber in Lae, with a focus on modern meeting facilities, better seating and improved support for media coverage.

Governor Rainbo Paita says the proposed improvements will address the current needs of the Morobe Provincial Assembly, including the installation of modern audio-visual equipment and a Hansard recording system.

The Hansard system will help record and keep an official account of discussions and decisions made during assembly meetings.

Paita says the work will focus on improving the interior meeting area, rather than renovating the entire provincial building.

The proposed improvements also include better seating arrangements and a designated space for media teams covering Tutumeng meetings.

The project has AUSAID support, with further assessment and scoping required to determine the work needed and the funding arrangements.

Paita says improving the facilities is important to ensure the Tutumeng chamber can properly support assembly meetings and the work of elected leaders.

Meanwhile, the Morobe Provincial Government is also planning a separate development at Kundu Park, which is being considered as the site for a new provincial government headquarters.

The proposed development will include a new Tutumeng building, a hotel and provincial government offices.

Paita says funding has been approved to relocate and resettle people currently occupying the proposed development area.

The long-term plan is to develop the entire Kundu Park precinct into a new provincial government headquarters.

The Tutumeng chamber improvements and the proposed Kundu Park development are separate projects aimed at improving the facilities and operations of the Morobe Provincial Government.

item.title: PNG Censorship shifts focus online
item.description: Chief Censor Jim Abani speaking during the regional consultations on the policy recently (NBC News) Papua New Guinea is moving to strengthen its censorship laws to deal with harmful content on the internet and social media.
item.content:encoded:
Chief Censor Jim Abani speaking during the regional consultations on the policy recently (NBC News)

Papua New Guinea is moving to strengthen its censorship laws to deal with harmful content on the internet and social media.

Chief Censor Jim Abani says the proposed National Censorship Policy III will shift the focus from traditional censorship of physical materials to online content as more people turn to digital platforms for information and entertainment.

Speaking during the regional consultations on the policy, Abani said the current approach was no longer enough to address the growing amount of content shared online.

He said the new policy would focus on protecting internet users, particularly young people, from harmful material found on digital platforms.

Abani said the Censorship Office had submitted more than 33,000 websites containing harmful content to the National Information and Communications Technology Authority (NICTA).

He said NICTA had so far blocked more than 200,000 listed websites and would continue taking action to restrict access to harmful online content.

Abani said the policy would also address gaps in the existing regulations and provide a framework that responds to changes in technology and how people access information.

He said the Censorship Office was also working with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) to support the government's approach to managing online content.

Meanwhile, Minister for Community Development, Youth and Religion Jason Peter said the policy was important in protecting the younger generation from cyberbullying, misinformation and other harmful content circulating online.

Peter said false information shared on social media could mislead the public, making it important to ensure information available on digital platforms was safe and reliable.

He said the government wanted to create a safer online environment for young people and all Papua New Guineans.

The regional consultations are aimed at gathering views from government agencies, civil society groups, community leaders, educators, media representatives and other stakeholders to help shape the National Censorship Policy III.

item.title: ICCC Commissioner refutes fake Lae PMV fare schedule
item.description: Independent Consumer and Competition Commission (ICCC) Commissioner Roy Daggy has dismissed a fare schedule circulating on social media, describing it as fake and unauthorised. In an interview with NBC News, Mr Daggy warned the public against sharing the misleading document, saying it was not an official ICCC-approved fare schedule for Lae.
item.content:encoded:
Independent Consumer and Competition Commission (ICCC) Commissioner Roy Daggy has dismissed a fare schedule circulating on social media, describing it as fake and unauthorised.

In an interview with NBC News, Mr Daggy warned the public against sharing the misleading document, saying it was not an official ICCC-approved fare schedule for Lae.

"This is a fake document and not an ICCC-authorised schedule for Lae. There is no increase," Mr Daggy said.

He clarified that approved PMV fares for licensed and gazetted routes in Lae Urban were adjusted from K1.50 to K1.80, effective as of 30th.

Daggy stressed that the approved fare applies to passengers travelling along complete routes and does not permit PMV operators to charge additional fares for short-distance trips or cut routes.

He also reminded PMV operators that student concession fares must be applied to eligible students.

Meanwhile, the ICCC said rising fuel costs had prompted the Commission to bring forward the phased fare adjustment across Papua New Guinea.

The adjustment includes a 20 per cent increase in bus fares across centres and routes, as well as a 14 per cent phased increase in taxi fares, applicable to Port Moresby and other centres where taxi services operate.

The Commission said a complete schedule of interim adjusted fares for all centres would be published in the National Gazette.

The ICCC will also work with relevant authorities, including the Road Traffic Authority, Police Traffic Directorate and Provincial Administrations, to ensure compliance and enforcement of approved fares under the Prices Regulation Act and other applicable laws.

The Commission has urged the public and PMV operators to rely only on officially approved fare schedules and avoid circulating misleading information on social media.

item.title: Madang Government urged to support koniak farmers
item.description: Bilake Enape Waizepa hands over the vehicle’s key to Justin and his wife (NBC News) The Madang Provincial Government has been urged to support koniak farmers in the province, especially in terms of creating road access for them to bring their produce to the markets in town.
item.content:encoded:
Bilake Enape Waizepa hands over the vehicle’s key to Justin and his wife (NBC News)

The Madang Provincial Government has been urged to support koniak farmers in the province, especially in terms of creating road access for them to bring their produce to the markets in town.

The call was made by the Managing Director of Ocean Kava Limited, a local buyer and exporter of Koniak, Madang's very own Kava.

Bilake Enape Waizepa extended the farmers' call recently whilst presenting a new Isuzu dyna vehicle to a local farmer.

Mr Waizepa said many of the Koniak farmers come from remote villages that have no road links and transport remains their biggest challenge when trying to bring their produce into town.

"Koniak farmers come from very remote locations, unlike cocoa and copra farmers; most of whom have easy access to road transport. Some of our farmers carry their koniak and walk for 2 to 3 days before getting on a PMV or boat to come to town just to sell their produce.

"Koniak is now transforming the livelihoods of rural families in Madang. It is directly putting K3 million to K4 million into farmers' pockets annually.

"They, however; need a little push from the government, especially with transport assistance. For those farmers in Raikos and on Karkar Island, they need bigger boats to move their koniak bags to Madang town. The small boats are not safe during times of strong winds and high seas," Mr Waizepa said.

He added that Koniak farmers in Madang Province have not received any form of assistance from the government since they started some six to seven years ago.

Despite their struggles, Mr Waizepa continues to encourage them to work hard.

The company has created a partnership program with the farmers to help them purchase materials like roofing sheets, iron posts, farming tools and/ or vehicles, boats, and other necessities to improve their livelihoods in the village.

Last week, it gave away another truck to a farmer under the partnership program.

The company's owner and Managing Director, Bilake Enape Waizepa, handed over a brand new Isuzu dyna to farmer Justin and his wife under the partnership program.

Justin from Simbai grows Koniak in his wife's village, Basken on Madang's north coast, and has been selling to Ocean Kava for two years.

However, his farm income over the last two years has been kept by the company under the program until it accumulated to over a hundred and thirty thousand kina, enough to purchase an Isuzu dyna.

Justin and his wife drove away a happy and satisfied couple last Tuesday with their first vehicle.

They were the fourth vehicle recipients.

The first three farmers got a Toyota Landcruiser, an Isuzu Dyna, and an open back utility.

Mr Bilake told farmers who witnessed Justin receive his Isuzu dyna from the company last week that nothing is impossible if they commit themselves to what they do are doing.

He said, "Justin's story should serve as an inspiration to other farmers to continue to work hard."

Ocean Kava Limited is one of Madang's leading buyers and exporters with secured markets in Fiji, Australia, New Zealand, China, and other countries.

It currently exports up to 100 tonnes annually.

Waizepa, meanwhile; plans to build a koniak processing facility in the nation's capital in order to add value to the product and to help create employment for the young people.

He added,"Nothing is impossible if you trust yourself and put your heart whole heart into what you're doing."

Justin said that as a simple carpenter, he did not think he would be successful one day.

He thanked Ocean Kava for introducing the partnership program to farmers, a lot of whom are already benefiting from it.
